description: §19.8.3 handling form 1 (S451 R11) on a `lift` in a server function body (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"): `lift ?{…}.all() !{ _ :> [] }`. In a server function body `lift` is the function's result, so the caller receives the rows on success (`notes` → 1 row; `empties` → `[]`, no row is not a failure) and the arm's `[]` when the query fails to run (`gone` is declared but never created). Pre-S455 (g-impl1-handled-sql-lowering-defects-s455 item 1) the guarded `lift` lowered with its value DROPPED — no return was emitted, every caller received null (the `.length` read then threw, so all three cells stayed "init") — and the query was not attempt-wrapped, so a failure still threw.
rationale: §19.8.3: "**A `!{}` handler on the query** — written after the terminator (`.get()`, `.all()`, `.run()`), its arms match `SqlError` variants". §19.8.3: "**"No row" is not a failure.** A query that runs and matches nothing succeeds: `.get()` on zero rows returns `not`, and `.all()` on zero rows returns `[]`, in every context". The handler adds the failure path only; the success value is the unhandled query's.
